<!--

## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
In case freebox is disconnected, when HA starts, it tests if Freebox is accessible. If not, this is never retried even when Freebox reconnects.
This PR writes error logs instead of stacktrace, and moreover, it created the FreeboxDeviceScanner object without testing Freebox presence. Error handling is done in `async_update_info` method which returns an empty list if Freebox is not there

issue_context.title: When freebox is not connected, device tracking never works even when freebox starts
issue_context.body:

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened instead.
-->
I've a setup where Home Assistant controls freebox starting through power switch. So Home assistant starts before freebox. In this case, all device_tracker reported by freebox remain absent even when freebox has finally started.
This is due to the fact that freebox presence is checked before initializing the tracker. If not there, tracker is set to None and no more retry is done.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant release with the issue: 0.106.0
- Last working Home Assistant release (if known): 
- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.): raspbian
- Integration causing this issue: freebox/device_tracker
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/freebox/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
freebox:
  host: foobar.fbxos.fr
  port: 1234
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt

```

review_comments: Why are these lines removed and why is `async_connect` not used?

these 2 lines are the root cause of the problem. As we check if the freebox is there. If not, we return None and then scanner is never recreated by home assistant.
Returning a not None scanner will force HA to try to update. Error checking is done on device update instead
